data.current_summary: Render an HTML document to a PDF
data.current_description:
Send an HTML document and get the PDF back as a download.

Inline images, fonts and CSS as `data:` URIs. External resources (http,
https, file) are not loaded: a document that references one is rejected with
400, and the detail lists the URLs. Relative URLs are ignored. JavaScript is
not run.

Limits: 2 MB of HTML, 50 pages, and 20 seconds including time in the queue.
Without an API key, the limit is 8 seconds and one render runs at a time.

On a paid plan, set `pdf_variant` to `pdf/a-2b` or `pdf/a-3b` for PDF/A
output.

Works without an API key for 10 requests a day per IP address. With a
key, a rejected or failed call costs no credits.
data.description_suggestion:
Render an HTML document to PDF with optional PDF/A output.

Send an HTML document and receive the PDF as a binary response. Inline images, fonts, and CSS must be embedded as `data:` URIs. External resources (http, https, file) are not loaded; documents referencing external resources are rejected with a 400 error listing the problematic URLs. Relative URLs and JavaScript are not processed.

Limits: 2 MB HTML input, 50 pages maximum, 20 seconds total (including queue time). Without an API key, limits are 8 seconds and sequential processing. On paid plans, set `pdf_variant` to `pdf/a-2b` or `pdf/a-3b` for PDF/A-compliant output.

Rate limits: 10 free requests per day per IP address without authentication. Failed or rejected calls do not consume credits when using an API key. Successful calls cost 1 credit.
